items.title: Workplace Lead
items.description: ABOUT POLYMARKET Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future. We're growing fast — both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a Workplace Lead to own our physical space and what it feels like to work here. You'll report to the Head of People Experience and manage the Office Manager and Receptionist. On day one you're running NYC HQ — over the next year you'll build the team and systems to keep it running at 200 and 500 people, and lead a major office build-out. This is a strategic role, not an administrative one. You'll run the office like a product, constantly shipping improvements that make the space match the intensity of the work we do. You'll manage the team, the budget, and the vendors, and own how Polymarket's offices look and feel. Done well, the workplace becomes a reason people want to come in. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Keep NYC HQ running at a high bar every day: space, supplies, furniture, and vibes - Select and manage vendors (cleaning, catering, facilities maintenance) and own the workplace budget — plan it, track it, and find places to save - Make sure investors, candidates, and partners understand who Polymarket is the moment they walk in - Work with IT and Security on visitor management, room booking, inventory, and maintenance systems, and keep them working as we grow - Own workplace health and safety: routine checks, ergonomics, local compliance, and emergency preparedness including evacuation plans and drills - Work with Security on physical access and incident response, from building access to visitor protocols - Manage and grow the workplace team, starting with the Office Manager and Receptionists — set clear goals, coach the team, and hold a high bar - Write the playbooks and SOPs so the office runs well when you're not in the room - Own the in-office events program: happy hours, celebrations, and All Hands logistics - Partner with People on culture programming: swag, welcome kits, recognition, onboarding, and seasonal moments - Manage the landlord relationship and ensure the lease is honored, we're compliant with local ordinances, and we maintain a strong partnership with the building - Work with in-house designers and outside architects on timeline, permitting, furniture, and the move itself — delivering the new space on time, on budget, and with an exceptional experience for the team - Take on more sites and real estate as we grow, scoping and building out new space as Polymarket expands WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 7–10+ years in workplace, office operations, or facilities at a high-growth startup or tech company, including managing people - You've built a workplace function and led the team that runs it day to day - You've led a major office build-out or relocation - Sharp with budgets and vendors — you negotiate well and hold people accountable - You build durable systems instead of one-off fixes - Extreme ownership: when the AV dies mid-all-hands, you fix it and make sure it doesn't happen again - High taste and attention to detail — the office should look good and run well - A strong communicator who can talk to executives, engineers, and contractors and adjust to whoever's in the room - (Plus) Experience in fintech, crypto, or fast-moving startups - (Plus) Experience managing office build-outs in NYC specifically - (Plus) Event planning background, internal or external - (Plus) Familiarity with Notion, Slack, and modern workplace tools - (Plus) Experience partnering directly with People Ops/HR on culture programming BENEFITS - Competitive salary & equity - Unlimited PTO - Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage - 401k match - Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories PAY TRANSPARENCY Base salary range: $200,000 to $300,000 annually, plus equity and benefits. This range reflects a good-faith estimate for this position. Experience levels vary widely within a title here, so please reach out even if your expectations fall outside it. We're always happy to chat.

items.title: Business Systems Transformation Lead, Procure-to-Pay
items.description: About the Team The Finance Platform & Technology team builds and scales the enterprise systems, integrations, and automation that power OpenAI’s financial operations. We enable business agility, operational excellence, and financial controls across procure-to-pay, quote-to-cash, supply chain, financial planning, and asset management. We partner closely with Procurement, Accounting, Tax, Treasury, Legal, Security, Data, and Engineering to simplify complex processes, modernize financial platforms, and build AI-first solutions that scale with OpenAI. About the Role We are looking for a Business Systems Transformation Lead, Procure-to-Pay to own and transform the systems and processes supporting OpenAI’s direct and indirect procurement operations. You will lead the design, implementation, integration, and ongoing optimization of P2P capabilities across Oracle Fusion Cloud, Zip, and connected enterprise platforms, spanning procurement intake, supplier management, purchasing, receiving, invoicing, tax, payments, banking integrations, and cash management. You will bring deep functional and technical understanding of enterprise P2P systems, translating complex business requirements into scalable solutions while working closely with Procurement, Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and Engineering. You will help shape the P2P systems roadmap and make practical decisions about when to configure existing platforms, integrate systems, build internal tools, or automate workflows. A core expectation of this role is an AI-first mindset. You will proactively identify opportunities to eliminate manual activities, automate recurring processes, and build intelligent workflows using OpenAI technology, AI agents, MCPs, plugins, and AI-assisted development tools. We are looking for someone who enjoys solving complex business problems, is comfortable working hands-on across enterprise applications, understands system integrations and operational exceptions, and takes ownership from solution design through production support. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Own end-to-end P2P systems and processes across direct and indirect procurement, including intake, requisitions, purchase orders, receiving, supplier management, invoicing, payments, and cash management. - Lead the design, configuration, implementation, and continuous improvement of Oracle Fusion Cloud Procurement and Payables, Zip, and connected enterprise applications. - Partner with Procurement, AP, Accounting, Tax, and Treasury to translate complex requirements into scalable system solutions, configurations, integrations, and automation. - Drive P2P transformation initiatives, including guided buying, purchasing and invoicing modernization, supplier lifecycle management, payment processing, and transaction visibility. - Work with integration engineers to design and validate integrations using OpenAI integration framework, APIs, business events, and file interfaces; establish validation, duplicate prevention, monitoring, reconciliation, and safe recovery. - Support global tax requirements including sales and use tax, VAT/GST, reverse charge, self-assessment, and withholding; partner with Accounting on accruals, intercompany, FX, prepaids, and financial close. - Own and enhance payment processes, including bank integrations, payment-status monitoring, settlement reconciliation, and Oracle Cash Management. - Identify and implement AI-first automation using agents, MCPs, plugins, AI-assisted development, and vibe coding to build internal tools, dashboards, exception monitoring, and recurring-task automation. - Evaluate native Oracle/Zip configuration versus integrations, internal applications, and AI agents; lead testing, UAT, deployments, stabilization, and secure operational controls. - Own production support, continuous improvement, and the long-term P2P roadmap to reduce manual intervention, processing exceptions, and procurement cycle time. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 10+ years of experience implementing, supporting, or leading enterprise Procure-to-Pay systems and transformation initiatives, with meaningful hands-on delivery and production ownership. - Have strong Oracle Fusion Cloud Procurement and Payables experience across suppliers, requisitions, purchasing, receiving, invoice processing, accounting, and payments. - Understand direct and indirect procurement and their different purchasing, receiving, invoice-matching, inventory-related, and financial-control requirements. - Have experience with Zip or similar procurement intake and orchestration platforms, including approvals, workflow configuration, supplier onboarding, and integration. - Have delivered cross-functional P2P implementations spanning multiple applications, integrations, stakeholders, and downstream financial processes. - Understand OpenAI integration framework or comparable platforms, REST APIs, events, data mapping, transaction lifecycle, error handling, and reconciliation; collaborate effectively with engineers on troubleshooting. - Have practical knowledge of AP accounting, accruals, financial close, intercompany, multicurrency/FX, prepaids, and subledger-to-GL reconciliation. - Understand indirect tax requirements—sales/use tax, VAT/GST, reverse charge, self-assessment, withholding, and engines such as Vertex—along with payments, bank integrations, and cash management. - Demonstrate a practical AI-first mindset and experience building or deploying agents, MCPs, plugins, AI-enabled workflows, or AI-assisted/vibe-coded tools. - Use SQL, reports, APIs, and logs to investigate data issues, manage exceptions, validate system results, and maintain access and financial controls. - Work independently across Procurement, Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and Engineering; take ownership through go-live and measure improvements in accuracy, cycle time, manual effort, and controls. items.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer, Internal Applications
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! WHY THIS ROLE? This role is for people who love building tools for their coworkers. The Internal Applications team creates tools that help us create better models. In this role you will collaborate with internal stakeholders, which include annotators, ML researchers, product managers and more. Join our team of builders who create tooling that will pave the way for the next generation of large language models! AS A FULL-STACK SOFTWARE ENGINEER ON THE INTERNAL APPLICATIONS TEAM, YOU WILL: - Work with a small talented and enthusiastic team of software engineers - Contribute to delightful experiences for our user-facing products, meticulously crafting code for browsers and servers - Collaborate and grow with your engineering colleagues of all levels through direct pairing sessions, architectural designs, documentation and talks - Identify and remove roadblocks to enable your team to increase its engineering velocity. - Build resilient systems that are mission-critical - Keep up with the cutting edge and adopt new technologies to improve performance and reliability YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF: - You have experience shipping products with a large number of stakeholders - You’re comfortable with the front and back end of the stack, and have previously worked with Next.js, TypeScript, React, and Python - You have hands-on experience with complex SQL queries - You have excellent communication skills and believe that documentation is a great way to get feedback and discuss technical implementations and designs - You’re excited to add new technologies to your toolbox and use them where it makes sense - You have the ability to take complex needs and goals and develop easy to understand explanations for all audiences - You’re excited about AI and have the motivation to scale a company FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. Our Platform and Core Engineering teams build the systems that make Kraken secure, resilient, and scalable. Their impact isn’t measured by customer-facing features, but by the strength, correctness, and leverage of the foundations they create. These teams power Kraken systems behind the scenes — enabling product teams to move fast while meeting the highest standards for reliability, compliance, and security. Engineers design shared services, internal platforms, and critical infrastructure that support company-wide initiatives. They optimize for safety, scalability, observability, auditability, and operational excellence — often operating in regulated, security-sensitive, and risk-heavy environments where precision matters. We’re looking for engineers with deep systems ownership and an architecture-first mindset — builders who take pride in long-lived services, thrive in complex environments, and are motivated by strengthening the backbone of the crypto ecosystem. THE OPPORTUNITY - Design and implement robust Rust services and foundational libraries that power Kraken’s core infrastructure, prioritizing correctness, security, and long-term maintainability. - Write reusable, testable, and highly efficient code built for scale, observability, and operational resilience in production environments. - Collaborate on large-scale distributed systems architecture, shaping low-latency, fault-tolerant services that support global trading and internal platforms. - Work alongside hundreds of experienced Rust engineers, contributing to a high-bar engineering culture grounded in ownership, rigor, and craftsmanship. WHAT YOU BRING - 7+ years of software engineering experience - Experience building and scaling shared systems, internal platforms, and supporting multiple product roadmaps - Proficient in writing network services or asynchronous code in Rust - Have a security-first mindset during system design to ensure robustness - Demonstrate the ability to autonomously debug issues across the stack (OS, network, application) - Apply a solid understanding of distributed systems and technologies, including RPC protocols, Kafka, and Event-Driven Systems, to design scalable solutions - Collaborate effectively with product teams to gather requirements and constraints for designing appropriate systems - Take complete end-to-end ownership of systems and libraries Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. You’ll have the opportunity to coordinate with functional SMEs and work with a wide range of stakeholders, from design engineering and operations teams, TPMs, external industry vendors and partners to ensure that all products are developed and delivered on time and to the highest quality standards. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees In this role, you will: - Own the integrated manufacturing and quality readiness for a product across L6, L10, and L11, with clear gates, milestones, deliverables, owners, and closure criteria. - Lead readiness of process flows, tooling, fixtures, assembly operations, test interfaces, and production controls. Maintain traceable evidence that assigned products and processes meet agreed performance, reliability, and compliance requirements. - Own the supplier and line scorecard. Make any unmet criteria clear to the responsible approval owners. - Manage multiple projects, track progress against milestones, communicate priorities and risks across functions, and coordinate risk mitigation to meet schedules and quality standards. As a Product Manager II on the Growth team within the Consumer & Business group, you'll own the end-to-end notifications platform spanning push, in-app, and email channels. items.title: Manufacturing Engineer, Motors & Actuators
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking Manufacturing Engineers to lead the development of processes, tooling, and prototype builds for custom motors and actuators. You will own a primary area as a Stator Process / Manufacturing Engineer, Tooling / Fixture Engineer, or Prototype Manufacturing Engineer, taking that work from early development through validation and repeatable execution in close partnership with mechanical, electromagnetic, electrical, test, quality, and supplier teams. These roles focus on the development, integration, and validation of electromechanical manufacturing capabilities, including stator winding processes, assembly and inspection tooling, and actuator prototype builds. You will help translate engineering designs into reliable hardware while establishing scalable processes, equipment, and build practices for future robotic platforms. This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 5 days a week. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL Each opening focuses on one of the three specialties below, with shared responsibility for reliable processes and hardware. - Stator Process / Manufacturing: develop and validate stacking, winding, termination, and potting processes. Establish process parameters, work instructions, and defect controls that produce consistent results across trained operators. - Tooling / Fixture: design and deliver winding tools, assembly fixtures, inspection gauges, and bench equipment, from CAD and drawings through fabrication, commissioning, and troubleshooting. Improve setup time, labor, and repeatability. - Prototype Manufacturing: plan and execute builds of existing actuator designs, from parts readiness and work instructions through inspection, approved rework, and delivery of complete actuator assemblies ready for robot integration. Resolve supplier and process issues, track failed parts, and use labor and yield data to improve subsequent builds. - Integrate and troubleshoot equipment within your specialty, working through operator workflow, material flow, and controls or test interfaces. - Resolve defects and bottlenecks through measurements and controlled trials. Demonstrate improvements in build time, repeatability, yield, and quality against defined acceptance criteria. - Release clear process and tooling documentation, maintain revisions, and train technicians and operators to reproduce successful results. - Work with mechanical designers to improve manufacturability while preserving approved magnetic, electrical, and safety requirements. Own the tooling designs and drawings needed to build and inspect the hardware, and coordinate product geometry, tolerance, and drawing changes with the product-design owner. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have personally developed, built, or improved manufacturing processes, tooling, or electromechanical assemblies, and can explain the engineering decisions and results you owned. - Move comfortably between hands-on troubleshooting, technical analysis, and working with technicians, operators, and suppliers. - Use measurements and experiments to distinguish part variation, tooling problems, process settings, and operator effects. - Choose equipment and automation with sound judgment about production rate, flexibility, cost, safety, and maintainability. - Set practical build or development priorities, communicate blockers early, and work across design, controls, test, quality, and operations to resolve them. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Relevant experience depends on the specialty: - Stator Process / Manufacturing: stacking, winding, termination, potting or cure processes, and winding or handling tooling. - Tooling / Fixture: fixture design, CAD and manufacturing drawings, metrology, equipment commissioning, and repeatability studies. - Prototype Manufacturing: electromechanical assembly, build planning, parts readiness, inspection, rework, testing, and delivery of complete hardware builds. - Motor, stator, actuator, or comparable electromechanical manufacturing experience. - Automated assembly, inline inspection, end-of-line testing, or equipment fault recovery; familiarity with sensors, PLCs, I/O, or pneumatics. - Process capability, measurement-system studies, and structured experiments. - Interest in using AI to simplify repetitive engineering work, with sound review of its outputs.
